To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Cross‐modal and non-monotone neural responses to uncertainty in statistical regularities are widespread and can be identified using multivariate pattern analysis.”

We found that neural responses to auditory, visual, and audiovisual stimuli varied with the degree of input regularity, and that these effects generalized across sensory modalities and across levels of input regularity in a non‐linear fashion.
we used multivariate pattern analyses to identify neural signatures of cross-modal and non-monotonically encoded input uncertainty in the human brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain encodes the regularity in the environment.
the neural basis of statistical learning, and the way the brain uses statistical information to make predictions about the environment.
the question of how the brain learns about the statistical structure of sensory inputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

The present study demonstrates that the brain encodes uncertainty non‐monotically and cross‐modally in multiple brain regions, and that conventional paradigmas testing for monotonic uncertainty responses may have limited generalization potential".
the brain is capable of encoding statistical regularities in a cross‐modal and in a non‐ monotonic fashion, but the neural mechanisms underlying this capacity remain to be elucidated.
the brain is not only capable of detecting regularity in the environment but also of representing it in a cross‐modal fashion and in a non‐linear way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified brain regions that are sensitive to input uncertainty, and that this sensitivity is both cross‐modal and can be non‐monotone.

the brain is not a simple monotonic machine, and that the encoding of statistical regularities in sensory inputs is not limited to a single modality, and that the neural representation of uncertainty is not monotonic.
the brain uses a variety of strategies for tracking statistical regularity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural representation of statistical regularity in the environment can be non‐monotonical, and can be cross‐modal.
the brain encodes input regularity in a non‐linear, non‐monotone fashion, and in a way that is not limited to a single sensory modularity.
the brain encodes uncertainty in a non-monotonic fashion, and that this encoding is cross-modal.
